clue.text: Graduate in Arab clothes for masquerade

indicators.note: to masquerade is to appear in disguise, so these letters turn up rearranged in another form

explanation.surface: A new graduate goes to a costume party wearing Arab dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'masquerade' looks like the party the clothes are for, but it is the anagram signal: ARAB CLOTHES FOR, all fourteen letters, rearranges to the degree.
explanation.definitionFit: A holder of a first university degree in the humanities is a graduate.

clue.text: Land reform as a ritual

indicators.note: to reform something is to reshape it, so these letters are formed anew

explanation.surface: A country remodels itself as if performing a ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' signals an anagram of AS A RITUAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The country and continent is a land, a sovereign territory.

clue.text: Women in household of sheikh are monitored

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: The women of a sheikh's household are kept under watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals letters lying inside the words: sheiKH AREMonitored.
explanation.definitionFit: The women of a Muslim household, kept in separate quarters, are collectively the women of that place.

clue.text: Holiday centre in so-called resort — in a particular place

indicators.note: in places the middle letter inside the rearranged letters
to re-sort is to sort again, so the letters of the word before are rearranged
centre points to the single middle letter of the word holiday

explanation.surface: A holiday spot in a so-called resort town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like the holiday place but signals an anagram: SO-CALLED becomes LOCALSED, and 'in' puts I, the centre of 'Holiday', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something confined to one spot or region is restricted to a particular place.

clue.text: Province or true capital of Malaysia

parts.note: real and true both mean genuine

indicators.note: the capital, or first letter, of the word Malaysia is wanted

explanation.surface: Asking whether a region is the real capital of Malaysia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital of' looks geographical (Kuala Lumpur) but means the capital letter M.
explanation.definitionFit: A kingdom or sphere of activity is a province in the sense of a domain.

clue.text: Fish struggles helplessly

definitions.meaning: flatfish such as the plaice-like species found in shallow seas
to stagger or blunder about clumsily

explanation.surface: A fish thrashes about helplessly.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a kind of flatfish and the verb means to flail or falter clumsily.

clue.text: What a poker player might do better?

definitions.text: What a poker player might do better?

parts.words: What a poker player might do better?
parts.note: a player who outbids another at cards increases the stake, and increasing is doing better

explanation.surface: Asking how a card player could improve their game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do better' reads as play more skilfully, but means to top the previous bet.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker, upping the bet beyond the last stake is literally going one better than it.

clue.text: Elizabethan poet starting sonnet writes to Queen Elizabeth

indicators.note: starting picks the opening letter of the word sonnet

parts.note: pens means writes
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher of Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: An Elizabethan poet begins a sonnet and sends it to the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabetha Regina, Latin for Queen Elizabeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund, author of The Faerie Queene, wrote in Elizabeth I's reign.

clue.text: One bridge player doesn't have trousers

parts.note: in bridge the four players are North, South, East and West, so S for South
lacks means is without, does not have

explanation.surface: A card player is caught without their trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four seats are named by compass points; S is South.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose casual trousers are a garment for the legs.

clue.text: Used in hospital, a service able surgical tool

indicators.note: used in says the letters are contained within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A surgical instrument that works well is used in hospitals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Used in' signals letters inside: hospitaL A SERvice.
explanation.definitionFit: A focused light beam device cuts and cauterises tissue, so it serves as a surgical instrument.

clue.text: Aromatic plant discovered by an American mother in the country

indicators.note: in puts these letters inside the country

parts.note: Chile is a country in South America
an gives A
mom is the American spelling of mum

explanation.surface: An American mother finds a fragrant herb while abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered by' is only a link; 'mother' with 'American' points to the US spelling, not mum.
explanation.definitionFit: The daisy-like herb used for tea is a fragrant plant.

clue.text: Beast swallowing a never ending sweet

indicators.note: swallowing means the animal takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: a camel is a beast of burden

indicators.note: ending picks the final letter of the word never

explanation.surface: An animal gulps down a sweet that never seems to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'never ending' reads as everlasting but gives only R, the end of 'never'; A and R go inside CAMEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A chewy toffee-like confection is a sweet.

clue.text: Title used when entertaining princess? It's a matter of etiquette

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so the title holds the princess inside

parts.note: Mrs is a title for a married woman
Anne is the Princess Royal

explanation.surface: Wondering which form of address to use when hosting royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: Princess Anne, the Princess Royal, is a crossword staple; 'when entertaining' puts ANNE inside MRS.
explanation.definitionFit: Polite behaviour or social customs are the substance of etiquette.

clue.text: Dictator in Rome backing everything American

indicators.note: backing means the pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: A Roman dictator supports everything American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support but turns ALL US backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucius Cornelius, a Roman general, made himself dictator of the Republic.

clue.text: One setting out unto a star?

definitions.text: One setting out unto a star?

indicators.note: setting out means laying out anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone setting off towards a star.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition and the wordplay: UNTO A STAR rearranged is a space traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: A space traveller is someone who sets off towards the stars.

clue.text: Squadron leader's advantage before North African battle

indicators.note: before says the advantage comes ahead of the North African
the leader of a word is its first letter, here of squadron

parts.note: an edge is an advantage
a Moor is a North African

explanation.surface: A squadron leader gains the upper hand before a desert battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squadron leader' looks like an RAF rank but gives S, its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1685 clash in Somerset that ended Monmouth's rebellion was an English battle.

clue.text: Outcasts tied up by river

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: roped means tied
the Tees is a river in north-east England

explanation.surface: Exiles are bound up beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ROPED to DEPOR; the TEES is a river in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: People expelled from a country are outcasts.

clue.text: What Lehar composed -a septet or orchestration

indicators.note: orchestration arranges music, here arranging these letters

explanation.surface: A septet arranges music by Lehar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orchestration' signals an anagram of A SEPTET OR; Franz Lehar wrote The Merry Widow.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Lehar wrote light comic operas such as The Merry Widow.

clue.text: Rose suddenly, after start of summer, made more showy

indicators.note: after says the showy phrase follows the letter
start of picks the first letter of the word summer

parts.note: tarted up means made gaudier or showier

explanation.surface: Someone jumped up and dressed up once summer began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like a flower but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To jump up or move with a sudden start is to rise suddenly.

clue.text: Braggart tersely announcing close of play?

definitions.meaning: a curt notice that a performance is cancelled or finished: the show is off

explanation.surface: A boaster curtly calls the end of a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A braggart is a boaster who flaunts himself; read as two words it curtly says a play is cancelled.

clue.text: Small fruit or piece of asparagus

parts.note: a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: Choosing between a small fruit and a vegetable stalk.
explanation.definitionFit: A single shoot or stalk of asparagus is called by this name.

clue.text: The effect of a break taken about the middle of July

indicators.note: taken about means the break goes around the other letters

parts.note: a rest is a break

indicators.note: the middle of picks the two central letters of July

explanation.surface: A holiday taken in mid-July has consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken about' says the break wraps round the two central letters of the month.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcome or consequence is the effect of something.

clue.text: Colour of doubloons? (3, 4) 2550% more required by an individual not getting on with field workers

parts.note: doubloons were Spanish coins of aged yellow metal, so their shade is a dull antique yellow

explanation.surface: Asking what shade pirate treasure is.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull brownish-yellow shade resembles antique coins of precious metal.

clue.text: Dismal doctor gets audience

parts.note: an ear is a hearing, an audience

explanation.surface: A gloomy doctor gets a hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Dull and gloomy, the word is a poetic synonym of dismal.

clue.text: Tool for making holes in cloth

explanation.surface: A boring tool goes into fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a boring tool and a twilled cotton fabric.

clue.text: 50% more required by an individual not getting on with field workers

indicators.note: fifty per cent of the word more is its second half

parts.note: an gives A

indicators.note: not getting means the following letters are dropped from the person

parts.note: a person is an individual

explanation.surface: Half as many again are needed by someone who cannot get along with farmhands.
explanation.walkthrough: '50%' takes the last half of MORE, RE; 'not getting' removes ON from PERSON.
explanation.definitionFit: Harvesters cutting grain are workers in the fields.

clue.text: Misbehave and take part in heightened drama?

definitions.meaning: to perform on a raised stage

explanation.surface: A child playing up in an over-the-top play.
explanation.definitionFit: To behave badly is to play up; read literally it means to perform raised up.

clue.text: Worker (one with aspirations, without aspiration) gets musical backing

indicators.note: an aspiration is the breathy sound of the letter H, so it is dropped

parts.note: a hoper is someone with hopes

indicators.note: backing means the musical is read in reverse

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical

explanation.surface: A worker with ambitions joins the chorus of a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aspiration' is used twice in two senses: hopes, and the H sound; dropping H from HOPER leaves OPER, then 'backing' turns EVITA.
explanation.definitionFit: A factory hand or secret agent is a worker.

clue.text: A little child with a large sum

parts.note: a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A small child holding a large amount of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A whole amount added up is a sum.

clue.text: Excellent job (for primary school teacher) for the price of a stamp

definitions.text: for the price of a stamp

parts.note: first-class means excellent
a post is a job

explanation.surface: A top job, teaching the youngest pupils, costs only a postage stamp.
explanation.walkthrough: The parenthesis is a joke: a primary teacher's job could be the first class's post. In Britain, letters go first or second class, priced by stamp.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail sent at the faster British postal rate costs one premium stamp.
